items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: Nazarro turned around to Mr. Ziegfeld, God rest his soul, turned around and said, Gene Buck, give them a contract.

ctx.x: I said, 'Well, I never like to interfere with the business part, but if Mr. Ziegfeld can only pay five and you're asking for $750, I'll say $800, just like that. Did you hear what I said? I could have said thousand just as easy as I said eight. But I already heard what the show -- who wants to do the show, and what I'll do the show for and so-and-so-and-so. And it ain't no bargain at $500, I can make $500 any time from this guy I'm working for. See what I mean? So to me, I can just raise it another $50 anyway and…

sold me, neither one. The man who is going to hire me is going to pay me more money than what he said and more money than what Nazarro said. See what I mean? So I got past that one and Nazarro turned around to Mr. Ziegfeld, God rest his soul, turned around and said, Gene Buck, give them a contract. Just like that. Give us a contract.

We go in this show, man, and never look back. Never look back. It was the greatest show that we ever had in life. Greatest showtime, because we did the shows and the shows were so pleasing that we stood out like a sore thumb, you know. We were the only ones that had vagabond clothes on in the show. We were the only ones that had dancing of the style that we were doing it, 'cause Mitzi Mayfair was a dancer and so was Harry Leroy, but they were a different style. I had the down-to-earth style, you see and they…
